turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today? How can I assist you?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. [Your Name]. Well, I'm here because... lately, things have just felt a bit much at work. I'm a teacher, and recently the district decided to add this new bilingual social-emotional learning program to my plate, right on top of my usual classes. 

I mean, I'm still getting through the day, but I just feel so wound up. And discouraged, honestly. It's really not like me. I've even started putting off my lesson plans and ignoring emails that I used to just handle without a second thought. I just don't feel like myself right now.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient describes developing emotional symptoms (feeling wound up and discouraged) and behavioral changes (procrastinating on lesson plans and emails) directly in response to an identifiable work stressor.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with family and friends?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I still enjoy spending time with my family, and... well, my hobbies haven't really changed. It's really just the work situation that's getting to me. When I'm away from the school and just at home, I still like doing the things I normally do. I haven't lost interest in that part of my life.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies any loss of interest or pleasure in usual activities, stating they still enjoy hobbies and time with family.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any physical symptoms lately, like trouble sleeping, feeling restless, fatigue, or muscle tension, that might be related to how stressed you've been feeling?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't really noticed any physical symptoms like that. I'm sleeping fine, and I don't feel particularly fatigued or restless. My body feels normal, it's just my mind that feels overwhelmed by the extra workload.

symptom_reasoning.S027: The patient explicitly states they are 'sleeping fine,' denying sleep disturbance.
symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient explicitly denies fatigue, stating they 'don't feel particularly fatigued.'
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient reports they do not feel 'restless' and that their body feels normal.
symptom_reasoning.S061: The patient directly denies experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension asked by the doctor, stating their 'body feels normal.'
